editorial:
Design for Living (Paramount, 1933) is Ernst Lubitsch's pre-Code comedy with Fredric March, Gary Cooper and Miriam Hopkins. It is adapted from Noël Coward's 1932 play, with a screenplay by Ben Hecht. A woman cannot choose between two men, and the three agree to live together platonically. Its pre-Code reputation makes it attractive for film-history, Lubitsch or Hecht retrospectives and for clips.

It is not free to use. The film was registered on 28 Dec 1933 and renewed on 29 Dec 1960 by Emka, Ltd. as R268586, as the Catalog of Copyright Entries for 1960 records. Copies on the Internet Archive or other sites show only that someone uploaded them. They do not make the film public domain. The Coward play underneath the film is a separate copyright, and I did not resolve its status.
faq: Is Design for Living (1933) in the public domain in the US?
No. The 1933 registration was renewed on 29 Dec 1960 (R268586, Emka, Ltd.), so the print is still under copyright. Free copies online do not change that.
Can I use clips from it if the film was renewed?

Only with permission from the rights holder, or under fair use, which depends on how the clip is used. Renewal means there is no public-domain route. The Coward play underneath is also a separate copyright whose status I did not resolve.
